# A call's side effects happen once, and they reach the caller, on the
# interpreter as on a compiled target.
#
# Two interpreter defects, each hidden behind the other. evalUserFuncCore took
# a declared return type to mean a pure body and ran it in a snapshot it then
# dropped, so a method that wrote a component var and returned a value wrote
# nothing: `bump()` in a click left `n` at 0. And a method call evaluated its
# arguments to find the receiver and then evaluated them again to bind them,
# so `add(next(), 0)` called next twice -- invisible while next's writes were
# being dropped.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component panel node {
    var n = 0
    var got = 0
    func next() int {
        n = n + 1
        return n
    }
    func add(x int, y int) => x + y
    button #bump(text="bump", @click {
        next()
    })
    button #sum(text="sum", @click {
        got = add(next(), 10)
    })
}

func testReturningMethodWritesState(t Test, c panel) {
    c.bump.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
}

func testArgumentEvaluatedOnce(t Test, c panel) {
    c.sum.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.got == 11)
}
-- testrun/bubbletea/go/app.sngl/panel/1 --

    {
      "Desc": "ArgumentEvaluatedOnce",
      "Passed": true
    },
    {
      "Desc": "ReturningMethodWritesState",
      "Passed": true
    }
  ]
}
